label: Richard Amesbury, Fideism §2.2.4, 'religion…: WITTGENSTEINIAN_FIDEISM_2, commitment 1: whatever…
locator: §2.2.4, 'religion is a self-contained and primarily expressive enterprise, governed by its own internal logic or grammar'
interpretation: The entry reports the fideistic interpretation of the later Wittgenstein: religion is 'a self-contained and primarily expressive enterprise, governed by its own internal logic or "grammar"', the view 'commonly called Wittgensteinian Fideism'. Read as: what the practice's own standards (its grammar) endorse is a correct move in it. Only that direction is formalized. The entry doubts that Wittgenstein endorsed the view; it is not attributed to him. Attribution reading of the position the entry reports, not a view of the entry's author.
attribution: The passage states that on Wittgensteinian fideism religion is a self-contained enterprise governed by its own internal grammar, which is the premise that what the practice's own standards endorse is a correct move in it.
